clue.text: Whip has nothing to say

indicators.note: to say means the word for nothing is spoken out, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A whip that has nothing to say for itself, or a person keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is northern English for nothing; the Russian whip KNOUT can be pronounced the same way, the K silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout is a Russian flogging scourge, a kind of lash.

clue.text: Staying calm, unlike Sir Thomas More

definitions.meaning: keeping composure under pressure, an idiom
More was beheaded by Henry VIII, so he did not retain the top of his body

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More, Henry VIII's Lord Chancellor, was executed by beheading in 1535.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means remaining composed, and literally means not losing the top of one's body.

clue.text: Looked sulky when deprived of power and ejected

indicators.note: deprived of means the letter for power is taken away from the word for looked sulky

parts.note: to pout is to look sulky, so looked sulky is pouted
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone sulked after losing their influence and being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outed is to be thrown out or expelled, a synonym.

clue.text: Time to hug, many times over

parts.note: to enfold someone is to embrace or hug them

explanation.surface: It is time for a hug, and a great many of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenfold means multiplied by ten, so increased many times over.

clue.text: Piece with a number of twists made for gripping pages

definitions.text: Piece with a number of twists made for gripping pages

parts.words: Piece with a number of twists made for gripping pages
parts.note: reads like a thrilling novel with a plot full of twists, but describes a bent bit of wire that holds sheets of paper together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Twists' and 'gripping pages' suggest a page-turning thriller; the object is a twisted wire that literally grips pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bent loop of wire used to fasten sheets of paper together, described literally.

clue.text: Drink up, seizing one vessel

indicators.note: seizing means the reversed word for drink holds the letter for one inside it
up in a down clue means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drinks up while grabbing a single container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAP into PAL, which 'seizing' wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, a container for carrying liquid.

clue.text: It's a long walk from Derbyshire 'to Scotland

definitions.text: It's a long walk from Derbyshire 'to Scotland

parts.words: It's a long walk from Derbyshire 'to Scotland
parts.note: describes plainly the famous long-distance footpath running up the spine of northern England to the Scottish border

explanation.walkthrough: The trail runs about 268 miles from Edale in Derbyshire to Kirk Yetholm just over the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's first national trail, a long-distance footpath along the hills of northern England.

clue.text: Stole away, ordered to find way to hide

indicators.note: to hide means the word for ordered conceals the abbreviation for way within it

parts.note: to rule is to decree or order, so ordered is ruled
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone slipped off, having been told to find a route to hide in.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal livestock, so rustled means made off with stolen animals.

clue.text: US resort began to slip into lake

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the word for lake

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake

indicators.note: to slip suggests the letters of the word began slide out of order

explanation.surface: Someone began sliding into a lake at an American holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to slip' turns BEGAN into NGBEA, which goes 'into' LOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Beach is a Californian coastal city and seaside destination.

clue.text: It's right to act for the benefit of others

definitions.text: It's right to act for the benefit of others

parts.words: It's right to act for the benefit of others
parts.note: sounds like a moral maxim about altruism, but describes a legal authority to act on another person's behalf

explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like moral rightness; it is a legal right, the authority granted by a document to manage someone's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal instrument giving one person authority to act for another in legal or financial matters.

clue.text: No starts made on adjacent boarding-house's new rooms

indicators.note: no starts means both words lose their opening letters

parts.note: next means adjacent, as in next door
a pension is a European boarding house

explanation.surface: A building plan allows no work to begin on the guest house next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No starts' takes N off NEXT and P off PENSION, leaving EXT and ENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an added part of a building, typically extra rooms.

clue.text: Tissue is replaced with fresh

indicators.note: replaced means the two letters of is are put back in a different order

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: Something old is swapped for something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, a band of fibrous body tissue.

clue.text: Can't be out in such cricket?

definitions.text: Can't be out in such cricket?

parts.words: Can't be out in such cricket?
parts.note: playfully suggests a batsman cannot be dismissed, while meaning the game cannot be played outside

explanation.walkthrough: 'out' in cricket means dismissed; here it means outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor cricket is a version of the game played inside a hall, never outdoors.

clue.text: Very little pressure on girl, we hear, to stop

indicators.note: we hear means the girl's name is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: Millie is a girl's name
to bar is to block or stop

explanation.surface: A girl is put under little pressure to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A millibar is a thousandth of a bar, a small unit of atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Initial child benefit entitlement

parts.note: reads like a state welfare payment for a child, but describes a right one holds from the moment of being born

explanation.walkthrough: Child Benefit is a UK state payment to parents; here 'initial' points to birth itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is a right or privilege inherited by virtue of one's birth.

clue.text: 'ad ringers organised to produce this?

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the two words are arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the h dropped as in casual speech

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers who had got themselves arranged produced a method.
explanation.walkthrough: In change ringing, bands of ringers are organised to ring set methods, one of which is this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandsire is a traditional method of change ringing on church bells, which ringers perform together.

clue.text: Ancient travellers fleeced on their way home

definitions.text: Ancient travellers fleeced on their way home

parts.words: Ancient travellers fleeced on their way home
parts.note: sounds like tourists robbed on their return trip, but refers to the Greek heroes who carried off the Golden Fleece

explanation.walkthrough: Jason and his crew sailed in the Argo to seize the Golden Fleece and bring it home.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's legendary crew aboard the Argo in Greek myth, who sailed to win the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: One's tiny daughter fine after life threatening event

indicators.note: after means the abbreviation for fine follows the word for the deadly event

parts.note: a war is an event that threatens lives
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A small daughter is doing well after a near-death experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwarf is a very small person or thing, so one who is tiny.

clue.text: Drink and' dope rejected by our group

indicators.note: rejected means the word for dope is turned back to front

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as is dope
us is the pronoun for our group

explanation.surface: Our group refuses both drink and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns GEN into NEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar and spice.

clue.text: Stow away and shortly visit island

indicators.note: shortly means the word for visit loses its final letter

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A stowaway makes a brief trip to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims SEE to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide or conceal it.

clue.text: I've finished discussing tautology

definitions.meaning: a phrase declaring the matter closed
the phrase repeats one word around a verb, saying the same thing twice

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a tautology because it just says something is what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase closes a conversation and is literally a statement of identity, saying nothing new.

clue.text: Exclude thus?

parts.note: an instruction to exclude can be carried out by closing a door on someone, keeping them outside

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a cryptic hint: excluding is done by closing someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut out is to keep someone out by closing a barrier, a synonym of exclude.

clue.text: Cushy job in vice, before copper comes in

parts.note: a sin is a vice

indicators.note: comes in means the chemical symbol for copper goes inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer moves into a comfortable post in the vice squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer heading for the vice squad; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post paying a salary for little or no work, an easy number.

clue.text: Volume added to old book

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid volume

explanation.surface: A further volume is added to an old book.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size formed by folding sheets into four leaves.

clue.text: Acknowledgment from radio officer getting excellent reception initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the five words in a row are taken

explanation.surface: A radio officer acknowledges a message received with good clarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is radio procedure for message received and understood.

clue.text: Heard range of food was reasonable

indicators.note: Heard means the word for the range of food is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: fare is the food offered, as on a menu

explanation.surface: The food on offer was apparently acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just or moderate, a synonym.

clue.text: Duet transposed key of piano piece

indicators.note: transposed means the letters of duet are moved into a different order

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A duet has been shifted into a different key for a piano work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposed' looks musical but rearranges DUET into ETUD.
explanation.definitionFit: An etude is a short instrumental composition, often for piano, practising a technique.

clue.text: Beauty magazine, perhaps, found in county no longer

parts.note: glam is glamour, beauty
an organ is a publication speaking for a group, a magazine being one example

explanation.surface: A beauty magazine is found in a former county.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan was a Welsh county, split up in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic Welsh county abolished in local government reorganisation, so a former shire.

clue.text: Have to wait -like a cigarette?

definitions.meaning: to linger or stay, a verb
full of tar, as cigarette smoke is

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a verb meaning to delay; the other is an adjective from tar, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means to linger or stay, the other means covered with or resembling tar.
